text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Travel agency Venus has declared bankruptcy leaving 400 clients stranded on Greek islands. It is the second travel firm to collapse in Denmark in the past week.
--Danish companies are set to beat previous records for acquisitions of foreign firms. In the first half of 1997 they bought 60 foreign businesses.
--Options Invest Danmark and Stock Invest have declared bankruptcy following regulators' refusal to grant them dealing licenses.
--The opening of direct rail services across the Great Belt bridge and tunnel link has not affected air travel between Copenhagen and towns on the Jutland peninsula.
--Mid-ranking Danish shipyards report healthy order books for both new construction and repair work.
--State railway DSB's freight division says it may have a 1998 loss of 100 million crowns, despite government aims of a break-even.
